transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Leo Martinez (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mendez (CTO - StrataBank), Anna Li (Head of Security), Thomas Reed (Platform Eng), Sophie Park (IAM Engineer)

Summary:
High-level security review focusing on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege mappings for an enterprise pilot. Discussed audit log retention, KMS/encryption key use for private deployments, and basic SOC2/ISO posture. Agreed next steps: exchange SAML metadata, run a live SCIM provisioning test, and align on RBAC role matrix for pilot.

Topics:
- SAML SSO integration flow and required attributes
- SCIM provisioning: groups & users, deprovisioning timing
- RBAC: recommended roles, least-privilege mappings, service accounts
- Audit logs: retention, access, S3 vs SIEM integration
- Encryption & KMS: customer-managed keys options for Private deployment
- Compliance: SOC2/ISO certs and evidence for customer review

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our SE who will walk through the SSO/SCIM bits, and Leo from CS.
[00:10] Carlos: Hi all, Carlos here, CTO at StrataBank, thanks for making time. We've got Anna and Thomas from security and platform, and Sophie our IAM lead.
[00:22] Anna: Hi, quick note: main goals are secure SSO setup, automated provisioning via SCIM, and ensuring RBAC maps to our least-privilege model. We also need to validate audit log retention for 7 years for certain regs.
[00:34] Priya: Great, thanks Anna. i'll start with the SAML flow at a high level — this is the SP initiated flow if you're doing web console SSO, we support standard saml 2.0 assertions, required attributes are email, name, and an optional groups claim for mapping. we also support nameid formats of email or persistent id.
[00:50] Sophie: okay, groups claim — does Redwood accept both string lists and comma delimited groups? our IdP is Okta but some teams use older stuff.
[00:58] Priya: we accept both in the mapping layer, there can be small parsing glitches in some older IdP configs; we'll send exact examples. sometimes the auto-map will create role mismatches, so we recommend pushing a group mapping table first.
[01:12] Thomas: what's the roughly expected SSO downtime or impact during enablement? we need to coordinate a maintenance window?
[01:18] Jordan: zero planned downtime for API-based calls; the console SSO switch is instantaneous; commonly customers do a staged rollout (canary) for a subset of users to validate mappings.
[01:28] Anna: can you confirm SCIM provisioning supports PATCH for partial updates and immediate deprovisioning on user disable? compliance wants immediate revocation when we offboard.
[01:37] Priya: yes, SCIM v2 with PATCH is supported, and we support immediate deprovisioning callbacks. note there can be a small propagation delay depending on our provisioning queue — typically under 30 seconds in Dedicated, under a minute in hosted. we'll include those SLA numbers in the doc.
[01:55] Carlos: when a user is deprovisioned, is their access token invalidated immediately? we have long-lived sessions to worry about.
[02:03] Priya: sessions use short-lived tokens for API access; web console sessions are configurable and we recommend 15 minute refresh for enterprise. for API keys, we recommend rotating service tokens and using RBAC-limited service accounts.
[02:18] Jordan: we should capture Thomas' note to inventory service accounts — that often trips customers up.
[02:25] Thomas: noted.
[02:28] Leo: quick question on SAML certificate rotation, do you support automatic SP cert rotation or do we need to re-upload metadata each time?
[02:36] Priya: we support re-keying with a rollover certificate; you can upload new SP certs in the console and there's a small window for dual-validity. we also support metadata hosting if you prefer a URL.
[02:48] Anna: audit logs — can you explain what levels of logs are available, where they're stored, and if we can stream them to our SIEM?
[02:56] Jordan: yes, we provide admin audit logs, auth events, and API request logs. retention is configurable; default hosted retention is 90 days, for Dedicated/Private we support longer retention and can export to S3 or push to your SIEM via syslog/HTTP forwarder. for regulated data, many customers use Private with a short-term cache and long-term S3 archival.
[03:20] Anna: we need at least 7 years for certain customer records. is that doable?
[03:24] Jordan: on Private deployments yes — you control the S3 lifecycle. on Dedicated we can negotiate extended retention as an add-on. we'll capture that as a contractual item for the pilot.
[03:34] Carlos: encryption — can we use a customer-managed key (CMK) in our cloud KMS? and for Private on-prem, what's the HSM story?
[03:42] Priya: for Hosted, we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, and CMK support via AWS KMS or GCP KMS is available for Dedicated/Private. for on-prem/HSM you'd deploy the provider integration and we support external key stores via KMIP / HSM integrations in our Private build.
[04:02] Sophie: any mention on who has access to KEKs in Redwood org? we need strict key separation and auditing.
[04:08] Jordan: access is restricted to the customer tenancy; Redwood engineering doesn't have access to customer CMKs. we can provide key access logs and attestations. we'll include a sample KMS access policy in the docs.
[04:18] Anna: SOC2/ISO evidence — what artifacts can you share? we need to feed these into our vendor assessment.
[04:24] Jordan: we can share the SOC2 Type II report under an NDA, ISO 27001 certificate, penetration test summary, and our security whitepaper. we'll attach links or provide them via the secure portal.
[04:36] Thomas: RBAC — show us recommended roles and how granular you can go with resource scoping. we want least privilege by default.
[04:44] Priya: our RBAC model is role-based with resource scoping. out-of-the-box roles are Admin, Operator, Viewer, Billing, and Service. you can also create custom roles with fine-grained permissions scoped to model, project, or environment. group-to-role mapping is via SCIM groups or SAML group claims.
[04:58] Thomas: can we have role constraints that limit model deployment to certain teams? e.g., only Platform can deploy to production models.
[05:05] Priya: yes, policy bindings let you restrict actions like deploy_model or create_route to groups. we also support approval workflows for deployment if you want a manual gate.
[05:16] Carlos: any way to do attribute-based access control (ABAC) today or is it roadmap?
[05:21] Priya: ABAC is on the roadmap; currently we do attribute-based mappings via SAML group claims and custom role definitions. full ABAC will be announced next quarter.
[05:32] Anna: about least privilege — do you support ephemeral role elevation for troubleshooting? we want to avoid permanent admin accounts.
[05:39] Priya: yes, we support time-bound role elevation via an approval step and paired audit logging. it's part of the Dedicated/Private offerings.
[05:47] Sophie: provisioning constraints — how fast do group membership changes reflect in permissions? if i remove a user from a group they shouldn't retain access.
[05:54] Priya: in most cases under 30s for Dedicated, up to a minute for hosted. tokens are short lived and we enforce on each request where possible. there's also a forced token revocation endpoint you can call on deprovision.
[06:06] Jordan: one common question: service accounts and machine users, we recommend assigning a minimal service role and rotate keys via Vault integration.
[06:15] Thomas: about rotation, can Redwood integrate with our Vault?
[06:19] Priya: yes, we have integrations with HashiCorp Vault for service token retrieval and rotation. we can provide example cookbooks.
[06:28] Leo: let me flag a small gotcha we see: group names in Okta with slashes or special chars sometimes break mapping — we'll send a normalization guide.
[06:36] Sophie: good to know. we have some legacy groups with odd chars.
[06:40] Jordan: next, let's cover audit log format and some example queries — Priya you want to walk through?
[06:46] Priya: sure — logs are JSON with fields for actor, action, resource_type, resource_id, timestamp, and request_context. here's a sample: {actor: 'sophie.park', action: 'create_api_key', resource_type: 'service_account', resource_id: 'svc-1234', ip: 'x.x.x.x'}. we'll include examples to ingest into Splunk or Sumo Logic.
[07:10] Anna: will you redact any PII from those logs? we can't have customer PHI in logs.
[07:16] Priya: we redact sensitive payloads by default and only keep metadata; payload redaction can be configured. for PHI-sensitive use cases we recommend Private deployments with in-tenant storage.
[07:29] Carlos: monitoring and alerting — can we get alerts for anomalous admin activity?
[07:34] Jordan: yes, we have alert hooks to push to PagerDuty/Slack and SOC teams; anomaly detection is a paid feature in our security add-on.
[07:44] Thomas: what's the onboarding timeline for SSO+SCIM+RBAC pilot? we need to be live with 50 users in the first sprint.
[07:51] Jordan: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: week 1: exchange metadata and create test tenant, week 2: provisioning and role mapping, week 3: validation and go/no-go, but we'll tailor to your timeline.
[08:02] Sophie: do you have a test harness for SCIM that we can run against before giving org wide access?
[08:08] Priya: yes, we provide a test sandbox and a SCIM sandbox endpoint. we also have a small harness script you can run — we'll share it.
[08:16] Anna: curious about data residency — can we restrict data to us-east-1? our legal requires certain records to stay in-region.
[08:23] Jordan: region restriction is supported on Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we have region options but not strict contractual residency unless Dedicated/Private. we'll go over region options in the follow-up.
[08:35] Carlos: low-latency concerns — does enabling KMS or extra logging affect latency?
[08:40] Priya: negligible for encryption envelope patterns; additional logging writes can add small overhead but the runtime is optimized for low latency. we'll include perf numbers.
[08:49] Thomas: for the RBAC mapping doc, can you provide an example CSV mapping group->role->resources? that will help our IAM team.
[08:56] Jordan: yes — we'll share a template.
[09:00] Leo: i want to call out the contractual item: extended log retention for 7 years will be a Dedicated/Private add-on; we'll capture that in commercial.
[09:10] Anna: fine, open to that.
[09:14] Carlos: what's the escalation path for security incidents? we need an incident contact and SLA.
[09:21] Jordan: we provide a security incident response process with 24/7 on-call for enterprise; typical SLA for acknowledgement is 1 hour and we'll provide the escalation matrix.
[09:31] Sophie: any special compliance checklist for financial services?
[09:35] Jordan: we have a finance vertical checklist — controls, encryption, audit exports, and vendor attestations. we'll send that.
[09:42] Thomas: small Q on SCIM: does Redwood support group nesting or is it flat membership?
[09:47] Priya: SCIM v2 doesn't standardize nested groups; our provisioning supports flat groups and we recommend flattening upstream or using attribute mapping.
[09:56] Anna: ok.
[10:00] Jordan: wrapping up — recap and next steps.
[10:04] Jordan: action items — Priya will send SAML SP metadata and SCIM guide, Jordan will share RBAC CSV template and SOC2 links, Sophie will provide IdP admin contact and test tenant info, Thomas will inventory service accounts. we'll schedule the live integration test next week.
[10:20] Carlos: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[10:25] Anna: thanks.
[10:28] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the integration test.
[10:35] (call ends)
